summary: We’re building Copilot as a new OS for work that spans every model, every form factor, and every task. Today, we’re announcing our biggest update to Copilot to date, bringing four things together: • Autopilot: proactive and long-running agent built for the enterprise • Code: build apps with Copilot, hosted inside your company’s tenant • Home: Chat + Cowork together • Office: now fully embedded in Copilot (and Copilot embedded in Office, of course!) Plus, you can invoke Copilot in Teams, and we’re introducing Today, a proactive experience that surfaces the most important information from across M365 without needing to ask for it. The way we work is changing and so are our workflows. This update brings AI into that flow, from answering a question, to building an app, to getting work done on your behalf. We’re building Copilot as a new OS for work that spans every model, every form factor, and every task. Today, we’re announcing our biggest update to Copilot to date, bringing four things together: **•** Autopilot: proactive and long-running agent built for the enterprise **•** Code: build apps with Copilot, hosted inside your company’s tenant **•** Home: Chat + Cowork together **•** Office: now fully embedded in Copilot (and Copilot embedded in Office, of course!) Plus, you can invoke Copilot in Teams, and we’re introducing Today, a proactive experience that surfaces the most important information from across M365 without needing to ask for it. The way we work is changing and so are our workflows. This update brings AI into that flow, from answering a question, to building an app, to getting work done on your behalf. [Thurman Brown](https://www.linkedin.com/in/thurmanbrownconsultant?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 6h


Satya, framing Copilot as a new operating system for work is a meaningful step, because the center of gravity is clearly moving from assistance to agentic execution. Microsoft is already building toward that future through Work IQ, Cowork, Scout, Agent 365, Entra, Purview, and multi-model orchestration. Microsoft now describes agents as active participants in work, with persistent identities, permissions, organizational context, and the ability to execute multi-step tasks across systems. From the Roots Informatics perspective, the opportunity is to add something complementary: an independent governance layer between Copilot’s intelligence and consequential execution. That matters because the more Copilot becomes an operating system for work, the more it will interact with systems that sit outside Microsoft’s own trust boundary—government databases, hospital systems, financial infrastructure, external APIs, robotics, sovereign data environments, partner clouds, and other model ecosystems. That is where Convergence — AI Infrastructure Between Intelligence and Action could strengthen Copilot. Microsoft already provides substantial governance inside its own ecosystem.
